newsitem.title: USA: Campbell in $2.5 billion stock buy-back, other initiatives.
newsitem.headline: Campbell in $2.5 billion stock buy-back, other initiatives.

text.p: A day after reporting its sixth consecutive year of record sales and earnings, Campbell Soup Co. said Thursday it was taking a number of "strategic actions," including a $2.5 billion stock repurchase plan and the elimination of about 650 jobs.
"We are poised for breaking away from our competitors in the food industry," Chairman David W. Johnson said in announcing the initiatives to securities analysts in New York.

The company said it will close or reorganize a number of manufacturing operations across North America, resulting in the elimination of 475 jobs. It will also cut 175 positions at its headquarters in Camden, N.J.
"Competition remains fierce," Johnson said, "so we must make strategic moves to maintain our leadership position and to grow Campbell to the next performance level."
Campbell's stock, which did not immediately begin trading Thursday when the New York Stock Exchange opened, shot up $4 to $71.50 shortly after it began trading.
Other announced actions include the acquisition of the Erasco Group, the leading canned soup company in Germany, which ranks as the largest commercial soup market outside the United States.

"Together with other businesses, Erasco will accelerate our growth throughout Germany and across the European Union," Johnson said. Campbell is buying Erasco from Grand Metropolitan Plc of Britain for about $210 million.

"This strategic growth plan is designed to vault our company into the ranks of the world's renowned consumer goods companies, in terms of financial profile and market multiple," said Johnson, who is also president and chief executive of Campbell.

"Armed with our powerhouse brands, we are moving forward with a full-scale strategic growth plan," added Johnson, who has sought to cut costs and improve efficiency at Campbell since he was named chairman in 1993.

Johnson said funding for the planned growth will come from several initiatives, including the sale of non-strategic businesses, a reorganization of manufacturing operations and reductions in administrative and staff functions.
These moves will result in an after-tax charge of about $160 million this fiscal year and will result in savings of $200 million over the next two years, Johnson said.

The company will also make a number of product and marketing changes to spur growth, he said. These include a new line of premium ready-to-serve soups, new frozen soups and faster roll-out of the Franco American Superiore range of premium canned pasta products.
Campbell will also introduce a Swanson Broth in resealable cartons, launch Pace Mexican sauces in Germany and undertake a joint venture for Godiva Chocolates in Japan, Johnson said.
In addition, Campbell announced plans to increase its advertising spending substantially, mainly for its soups, Pepperidge Farm snacks, V-8 vegetable juice and Swanson frozen foods.

Johnson said Campbell's board had authorised the repurchase of up to $2.5 billion worth of its stock, starting with a one-time tender offer for up to $1.5 billion, followed by an open market purchase of another $1 billion.
The company said it will announce the details of the so-called "dutch auction" stock repurchase plan next week.
On Wednesday Campbell said its profits grew by 15 percent to $802 million for the year ended July 28 as sales expanded by 6 percent to $7.68 billion.
